label: paragraph_title
text: LISTENING IN.

label: paragraph_title
text: Application Made to the Government.

label: text
text: A scheme is at present before the Government by which the owner of the smallest wireless set in Hongkong may "listen in" to music, lectures, etc.

label: text
text: The “China Mail” announced some weeks ago that the Government had decided that it could not be directly responsible for any system of broadcasting in Hong Kong and indicated that it was up to local radio enthusiasts to make their arrangements accordingly.

label: text
text: Shortly after this announcement a meeting of the Radio Society was held at which it was understood that efforts were to be made to fit up a transmitting set. These efforts, the "China Mail" understands, have not borne fruit yet, owing to the difficulty of getting a licence from the Government, whom it would appear is anxious to have a guarantee of more or less permanency in connection with such a service before it feels disposed to grant a licence.

label: text
text:
Meanwhile the Y.M.C.A. have submitted a scheme and made application for a licence in connection with a scheme for broadcasting lectures in Chinese and English, also suitable music, many of their supporters having advocated the provision of some such facilities. The Greater China Radio Co. are prepared to guarantee the provision of a Westinghouse transmitting set at the Y.M.C.A. headquarters and the scheme is likely to develop if the Government will grant the licence which has been asked for.
In connection with this latter particular, which has been the stumbling block in connection with the scheme of the Radio Society, a “China Mail” representative who made enquiries was informed that there would be no objection provided that regulations were complied with. The regulations are now being prepared.

label: text
text: According to a telegram received at the General Post Office from Shanghai, the mails to Europe via Siberia will in future close at 9 p.m. on Tuesdays at the Shanghai Post Office so as to connect with the trans-Siberian express at Harbin on Monday of the following week. The local mails will therefore be despatched by the latest boat to keep up with the new schedule. The unsatisfactory conditions which have hitherto existed owing to traffic dislocations when it has been necessary to connect at Harbin will be eliminated under the new arrangements and the Siberian route should now prove more popular.

label: text
text: The London letters and papers dated April 24 by the Siberian route arrived this morning by the s.s. Eiberfeld. The mail was a large one comprising 170 bags, of which the United Kingdom sent 35: Switzerland, 4; Holland, 2; Vienna, 9; Italy, 4; and Germany 18.

text: The most interesting case was that in which four men appeared in the dock charged in connection with a robbery from a woman on Victoria Road. A taxi cab driver was mixed up in this, having driven up while the robbery was proceeding. On being intimidated he drove away. The woman made a fight of it but was overpowered, knocked down, and had a bangle taken from her.

label: text
text: At an extraordinary general meeting of the Hongkong and Whampoa Dock Company, Ltd., held this morning, the proposals for increasing the capital of the Company were approved.

In the ratio of one new share for each old share that they hold and at a premium of $10 a share. The Directors are given power to dispose of any of the new shares not taken up, and also of the unissued 80,000 new shares in any manner they think fit.

A gang of four men, two armed with revolvers, entered the Man Pak Cheong shop at No. 47 Wing Lok Street, second floor, yesterday afternoon, and stole $700 from a safe after threatening the occupants. The robbers made a hasty exit before completing their work on one of the occupants evading them and giving the alarm from the verandah.
